prompt: What does the lesson say a quarterly review is?

choices.text: A display of everything the team measured
choices.why: That is the first draft's mistake.

choices.text: A short talk that ends in a decision
choices.why: Right. People who do not see the work decide something about it.

choices.text: A ranking of the team's developers
choices.why: Lesson 8 ruled that out.

choices.text: A report sent and never discussed
choices.why: The page is discussed in the half hour.

prompt: Which questions does the lesson say managers of several teams bring to a review? Choose every one that applies.

choices.text: Is it getting better or worse?
choices.why: The direction, and whether it is real.

choices.text: Can I believe your dates?
choices.why: Commitments to customers depend on it.

choices.text: What do you need from me?
choices.why: A decision, a budget, a person.

choices.text: Who is the slowest developer?
choices.why: Not a question a review should answer.

prompt: Why does the lesson keep the cumulative flow diagram out of the review?

choices.text: Because it is inaccurate
choices.why: It is accurate; it is the wrong instrument for this audience.

choices.text: Because it reveals too much
choices.why: Nothing in it is secret.

choices.text: Because the director asked for it to be removed
choices.why: Nobody asked; it is a judgement.

choices.text: It is a daily tool, opaque if seen once
choices.why: Right. Read once a quarter, it produces silence.

prompt: What question did Bia ask the director before writing anything?

choices.text: What will you decide then?
choices.why: Right. The answer changed what went on the page.

choices.text: Which charts do you like best?
choices.why: Taste is not the point.

choices.text: How long can I talk for?
choices.why: The length was already known.

choices.text: Who else will be in the room?
choices.why: Useful, but not the question that shaped the review.

prompt: Put the three sentences a chart must support, according to the test, in order.
Why did the chart of story points per sprint leave the review?

choices.text: Because it went down
choices.why: It went up and to the right.

choices.text: Because the numbers were wrong
choices.why: It was accurate.

choices.text: It supported no decision
choices.why: Right. It measured estimates, not anything a shop feels.

choices.text: Because Marta dislikes charts
choices.why: She asked a question; the chart could not answer it.

prompt: "Median cycle time: 4 days." What does the lesson say is missing?

choices.text: A chart instead of a number
choices.why: A chart of one number is decoration.

choices.text: The before beside it
choices.why: Right. "4 days, down from 23 in July" is a finding.

choices.text: The mean as well as the median
choices.why: The mean is not what the lesson asks for.

choices.text: Each developer's own time
choices.why: Lesson 8 rules that out.

prompt: Match each chart to the reason it fails the test.

pairs.right: a fully busy team is a slow team
measures estimates, not what customers feel

prompt: Why does the incident stay in the review even though it makes the team look worse?

choices.text: Because the law requires incidents to be reported
choices.why: The lesson's reason is not legal.

choices.text: To ask for a bigger budget
choices.why: The asks are about the freeze and the rota.

choices.text: Because the director requested it
choices.why: Nobody had to ask.

choices.text: It passes the test; omitting it costs belief
choices.why: Right. The room already knows about it.

prompt: Median cycle time fell from 23 days in July to 4 in September. By how many days?
Items finished per month were 32, 41 and 30. What does the lesson say about that?

choices.text: It finished sooner, not more
choices.why: Right. Said first, it prevents the commonest misreading.

choices.text: The team got slower in September
choices.why: September is back where July was.

choices.text: It should be left off the page
choices.why: It goes on the page because of the question it answers.

choices.text: August proves people worked harder
choices.why: August's bump was the board draining.

prompt: In September, 1 deployment in 20 failed. What share is that, in percent?
Why does the incident get its own line on the page instead of a cell in the monthly table?

choices.text: Because its minutes broken were the highest
choices.why: July's 195 minutes were higher.

choices.text: Because the table has no room
choices.why: Room is not the reason.

choices.text: The table hides what it did to shops
choices.why: Right. 55 minutes looks like 48 in a column.

choices.text: Because it happened in a different quarter
choices.why: It happened on 30 September, inside the quarter.

prompt: Which single chart does the lesson choose to carry the review?

choices.text: The cumulative flow diagram, every week
choices.why: A daily tool for the team.

choices.text: Cycle time by month, 3 Aug marked
choices.why: Right. The change, its size and its timing.

choices.text: Deployments per week, by month
choices.why: Two numbers and a sentence do that.

choices.text: The error budget burn-down
choices.why: The incident goes as text.

prompt: Why does the page go out the day before the meeting?

choices.text: So the meeting can be cancelled
choices.why: The meeting still happens.

choices.text: So nobody needs to attend
choices.why: The half hour is for questions.

choices.text: Because the tool sends it automatically
choices.why: Nothing automatic is described.

choices.text: People read faster than anybody speaks
choices.why: Right. The meeting is spent on questions.

prompt: Put the sections of the Billing team's page in order.
Why does the headline carry the bad news beside the good?

choices.text: Omitting it loses the room later
choices.why: Right. Somebody will mention it.

choices.text: To make the team look humble
choices.why: Humility is not the reason.

choices.text: Because good news is less interesting
choices.why: Both are there for the reader.

choices.text: Because the policy forbids good news alone
choices.why: No policy says that.

prompt: Why does the lesson prefer "23 days to 4" over "significantly improved"?

choices.text: Because adjectives are not allowed in English
choices.why: They are allowed; this one is a claim.

choices.text: Because numbers are shorter
choices.why: Length is not the point.

choices.text: It lets the reader judge for themselves
choices.why: Right. The adjective is a claim the numbers make better.

choices.text: Because the director does not read words
choices.why: The page is full of words.

prompt: The head of product proposes a target of 4 days for next quarter. What is Bia's answer?

choices.text: Agree, and promise 3 days
choices.why: That is the trap lesson 7 describes.

choices.text: Report the measure; target the practice
choices.why: Right. A cycle-time target can be met by gaming it.

choices.text: Refuse to report cycle time at all
choices.why: She keeps reporting it every quarter.

choices.text: Ask for a target on story points instead
choices.why: Points are worse, not better.

prompt: "Can you go faster?" Why does Bia not answer "we'll try"?

choices.text: Because the team is already the fastest
choices.why: No comparison is made.

choices.text: Because she wants more people first
choices.why: Lesson 12 warns against that.

choices.text: Because speed is not measured
choices.why: Throughput is measured, and it is flat.

choices.text: Flat throughput promises nothing
choices.why: Right. What the team promises is that it finishes soon.

prompt: A forecast's credibility is its track ___.
What did the director decide, and why does the lesson call it the best outcome?

choices.text: Two teams try the rules
choices.why: Right. A choice made on evidence, to be checked again.

choices.text: Every team adopts the rules at once
choices.why: Two teams try them first.

choices.text: The Billing team gets a bonus
choices.why: Not applause; a choice.

choices.text: The freeze is cancelled
choices.why: The freeze stands.

prompt: Deployments went from 5 in July to 20 in September. How many times as many is that?
Asked to compare the Billing team with the Payments team, what does Bia offer instead?

choices.text: A ranking of both teams by velocity
choices.why: Lesson 6 rules out comparing teams.

choices.text: A refusal to discuss Payments
choices.why: She offers something useful.

choices.text: Payments against its own July
choices.why: Right. Before and after, on the same team.

choices.text: Merging both teams' numbers
choices.why: That hides both.
